data: Amazing game replay value and worth every cent
overall the game is well worth the price
This game also has an excellent WIKI, one of the best I have seen, highly recommended to understand the game mechanics
10/10 best idle game out there, bless the dev
My only wish is that there were more than 6 character slots
DON'T WASTE YOUR MONEY ON THIS GAME
It’s bland, forgettable, and offers nothing that would make you want to return- unless you’re into grinding for the sake of grinding

The only reason that my playtime at the time of review is so low is because I can play this on my phone during staff meetings at work, and it saves to the cloud so you can resume progress here. 10/10 would definitely recommend as a time suck during the dull moments in life.

It's fun enough to check up on progress every now and then but it's not really a "game" in the sense that you cannot directly affect the result of anything by means other than waiting... It's more like watching paint dry than playing an RPG.

Absolutely not worth $10, not even $5. This game is free on the App store and IN BROWSER, yes the exact same game on the exact same platform but $10 cheaper.

For some reason there is a 12 hour timer so unless you keep the game open you have to keep coming back in order to make progress which is pretty dumb for something I would potentially be paying $10 for.

Save yourself the cash and google Melvor Idle. You can play for free in browser.
Very solid idle game, if you play a lot of idle game I recommend starting with adventure mode, it'll give you more of the experience you're looking for.
If you want to feel like your botting osrs this is the game for you

As someone with an embarrassing number of hours invested ("wasted" would be a more accurate term) in that other game, I think it's remarkable how close this one comes to scratching the same itch without the same level of pressure and mindless commitment.

Great idle game. As someone who loves osrs but can't afford the time it requires to meet goals, this game really scratches the decision making itch without the "sitting there for 10 hours to get to the next step of your journey" commitments runescape is full of.

This is a great idle game for me to go back and forth with other things. I can set the game up to grind a specific skill/item/monster, walk away for a few minutes to do dishes, then come back and heal up/switch tasks/etc.

For a busy body, this is an ideal game. I can also let it run on mobile while I'm in between other tasks as well. Offline growth is a plus. It also has a depth and longevity that I didn't expect. 

Overall this is a great game.

The concept and design are excellent. Unlike many idle games, there is even a story. Unfortunately, the story is poorly written, which makes what should be a positive a negative. This applies to the rest of the game as well. All of the details are ruined to some extent by sloppiness. The text is small and poorly laid out, making it difficult for people with poor vision. For people with problems seeing colors, the situation gets worse with items distinguished by various shades of gray or green. The Age of Discovery DLC is particularly bad and has numerous annoyances. Even small things like two buttons for the Archeology skill being on Archeology while the third is bizarrely on Cartography. This DLC does at least have item descriptions, something the developers couldn't be bothered to add to the rest of the game.

Sadly, everything in the game is like this. Sloppy and lazy.

Very fast progression to level 40, then it becomes excruciatingly slow.
Pacing becomes very poor.

Really good game to keep in the background while doing other tasks. Alot like runescape but without actual gameplay. I enjoy idle games and this is one that I boot up every time I log on before hitting my other games
So I've only played the game for a little bit but, looks very promising with lots of new stuff to come.
Runescape, but idle. Menus and progress bars instead of graphics. You can play on Steam, browser, phone.
Very nice and relaxing game. Similar to RuneScape but IDLE mode you guessed it :)

Everything is a progress bar.
My life is a progress bar, the years of my life are progress bars, waiting for the bus to come has become a progress bar, talking to my mom has become a progress bar, eating lunch, washing my hands, washing my ass, petting the cat, pegging the neighbour, sleeping, waking up, crying, pissing and shitting myself at the same time have all became progress bars.

Do not. Do what I have done.
Do. Not.

Minimal effort for maximum enjoyment.

P.S. Wiki good.

P.P.S. If you intend to get 100% achievements, create both Standard & Hardcore characters and let them idle concurrently.

Did you play OSRS? Do you long for the nostalgic feel of a feudal RPG without having to do any of the grind heavy lifting? This is the game for you. Out source wood cutting and cow slaughtering while you slave away at other things on your keyboard. This game does the Bot'ing for you, and I love it. Are you telling me I get to be around for all the cool parts? Like selling my inventory and crafting new gear. And not be around for the countless hours of tapping and moving around? That's right. This game keeps the items and pve encounters while taking the world out of it. Play, organize, and watch yourself grow.

Just starting playing this game yesterday, but I will keep you posted on the epic Dungeons that are about to ensue.

It's not very interactive or engaging, but it's kept me occupied much longer than other idle games. The key difference is the existence of end goals, rather than just pointless grinding ad infinitum. The game is 99% idle and doesn't demand attention to the point of annoyance. I don't find it nearly as enjoyable or as charming as Runescape, but it's familiar and not bad. Worth checking out if you like idle games, just don't expect much interactivity.
Great "Idle" game where you can set your actions, let it run and check back on it when you have time.
It is perfect to play on the Go or at home. Simple and lots to accomplish. Fun game.
I feel the nostalgia for playing RS and OSRS immensely while playing. Extremely addicting and so satisfying.

game interface is ugly. there is NO AUDIO! -_- all images look AI generated. game was lazily created.

no.

I bought this game hoping for a nice idler experience, as I like runescape very mucho.

I have to say the quality of life in this game is below average for the steep price. Inadequate linking in the menus makes it feel poorly designed even compared to mobile f2p games. Could be expanded upon for a more streamlined experience. But as it stands it needs to be baby-sit tremendously to the mind-numbing level of getting 99 flet or wc or fm or w/e in the main game xd
It runs quite RAM intensive, so I'd rather not leave it running.
Meh
It gets extremelly overwhelming after the first 30-40 hours. Its not the simple idle game you might expect. Not my cup of tea.
If you like RuneScape, you can skill while you skill. Great second monitor game for the nostalgic.
Great game! Been mostly playing it on browser and almost finished the base game. The native mod support is just awesome!
It's like Runescape but you don't have the time to sit and play Runescape. Progression feels really good and rewarding. It's kept me pretty entertained for almost a year so far.

Currently my new favourite Idle game, so much content and fun stuff to explore!
Update: Still going strong
Simple game for those who have the dreaded Runescape nostalgia but lack the time to indulge in it.

A deep and familiar idle game that will give you hundreds of hours of enjoyment as it is already, and is actively being improved by developers. I encourage you to at least try the browser version if you haven't tried it before. Excellent game.

Despite seeming to be a game with a rich and intricate systems, the game is pretty shallow. The interaction between skills, even those skills that exist solely to buff other skills, is lackluster. Also, many of the staple mechanics of incremental games, like prestiging, are just absent.

It's a nice game, and $10 is a fair price, but the game is rather lackluster on the whole.

backup your save manually as often as possible, did not realize the game does not use steams cloud save feature, but instead its own that you have to sign up for. Opened the game to realize that my level 700+ save is just completely gone and there is no way to get it back. Make an account for the cloud save or back up your save often if you plan on sinking alot of time into the game like I did

It is a somewhat grindy game I let it mine gold overnight then spent the whole day smithing it to bars and made over four million GP. 4/5 stars

Terrible pacing and questionable game design. Lot of tasks and things to unlock that require a chain of levelling other stuff up first (Like levelling your cooking skill just to cook the fish you caught, or levelling firemaking to unlock Agility courses). It makes doing what you actually want to do infinitely more tedious and less interesting. On top of all of this, the inventory management is horrendous. The game incentivizes you to keep items and equipment to trade in for tasks later, or you never know what will be used for a recipe you still have yet to unlock. So there is constantly an overflow of items and ambiguity of what is worth selling off.
When crafting, I also don't like how I can't specify how many times I want to craft something - like putting a limit on my actions. It makes having to baby sit the game feel bad when I only want a couple hundred of something made but have 1000's of materials...
Some stuff is very passive to level (Mining, Woodcutting, Astrology) while other stuff is very active to level (Combat, Farming, Crafting/Fletching/Smithing) which is a bit jarring for a idle game.
Overall not a bad game given it is an idle game however I was just expecting a bit more cohesion in the experience and less jank. This all being said I'm interested to see how Melvor 2 will be and if there are improvements to the game that I am looking for.

All the dopamining of Runescape and MMOs, without FOMO, microtransactions, or subscription fees! I loooove this game, especially since it respects my time. I can watch number go up and still be an adult with responsibilities. I played a long time ago, and the game has had a lot of improvements since then. I picked it back up and bought my bf a copy. He's been struggling with tendonitis in his forearms and this game is great for resting his wrists.

I enjoy that:
- Game is still actively worked on, latest update was this month
- Once I bought the steam version, I can access my cloud saves on the app or web client, without having to pay for the game twice
- Can import local saves, so I think it would be possible to move free account over

All my actual problems with the game involve the app performance, and are thus not applicable to this review of the steam version.

There are two kinds of people in the world: those who like incremental games and those who think we're absolute idiots. No prestige system, by the way, so if you want to scratch that itch you felt playing Kittens Game or Magic Research, look elsewhere. 10/10
Super fun Idle game that seems to never end. If you like Idle games, I think you will like this one.
Back in the day I used to play text RPGs and this is just that with a bunch of quality of life updates. HC mode makes it feel very exciting,

Haha, fun times... although I keep forgetting I have this running and suddenly I've cut down 50k trees and mine a whole mountain. Worst part about this game, it may end up being the most expensive game I've got in my library, as I may have to go and buy a third monitor, just so I can keep watching those lovely numbers go up, without sacrificing my Netflix or other gaming spaces..

Holy cow - This is legit just OSRS but as an idle game. With multiple enemies, multiple slayer tasks and plenty to keep your idle self goin! Farming, Smithing, Crafting the whole 9 yards is here. Earn Mastery ranks for each skill and get percentage bonuses based on how far your mastery has gone. Although some skills mastery will take much more time and manual(ish) time spent on them, like farming or crafting, you will delve so many hours into this its unbelievable. I bought this 3 days ago. I am almost to 55 hours at the time of this review.

Pro tip - Get your woodcutting skill maxed ASAP and rack in the millions of GP to come from Mother Nidle then work on other skills from there as you will have all the money you should need.

First major update was yesterday, and I cannot wait to see what additions/minigames get added. Grand Exchange when!?!

If you love Runescape or Oldschool Runescape, this is the perfect Idle game for you. ive had nothing but good things to say about this game, and its even been praised by Daddy Jagex themselves.

Melvor Idle is cross platform, you can save your game on pc, and pick back up on mobile and continue, or visa versa. Full version has plenty to do, 5 character save spaces, plenty of skills to master, bosses to defeat, Dungeons to delve, and items to obtain. ive been playing at the moment of writing for 210 days, 1 hour, 15 minutes. i know this because statistics like this are available to you in the menu.

game receives updates, adding more content or QoL features, supports "Cloud Saves" so you can back-up your account so you don't have to worry about file corruption or other hazards.

There's even things for the Completionists, the modders, the "treasure seekers", the Easter Egg hunters, And Pet Collectors. Skill capes(With PERKS!) including Max Cape, and Completionist Cape

Note* To get this game and all features, buy it here on steam, you will then be able to have the purchased/full version of the game available to you on mobile.
One of the best idler games our there. If you like the Runescape theme as well then this will be even better for you.

I played Runescape for 11 years of my life, but nowadays.. I just don't have time.

Or so I thought...

Melvor Idle gives you the opportunity to play runescape, in a text based form, all while spending time with family, working, sleeping, driving. It just keeps going. You don't have to dream about having 99 woodcutting and spend 8 hour days a day in your busy life clicking trees.. You simply press a button and walk away. 8 hours from then, log in and check out your 6k yew logs.

Beyond being just an idle runescape game, it has decent lore - a ton of new weapons and items that differ from the real game. I highly recommend this game if you enjoy a good idle game, and runescape.
If you make a game that has a gigantic memory leak that crashes the game every time, and then go on to make other games without ever fixing that memory leak... I'm not buying any of your other games.

better than the actual runescape idle

EDIT: 2000 hours later its still great. 10/10 best idle game out there, bless the dev

One of the most attractive and chill idle games out there...but also the perfect pandemic companion. I started this game at the beginning of the pandemic and told myself I wouldn't stop until the pandemic was over.

Well, here we are...nearly 9 months later...still going strong, and I still haven't unlocked all the capes. Thanks for bein' my boon companion and getting me through my lockdown depression, Melvor Idle. <3

I gave this game a try a while back when it was free on epic, and bounced off it due to the seemingly complex UI. I randomly decided to get a key from Humble Bundle for it since I have been into Swarm Simulator but wanted something with more depth and gave this a shot again. I will preface this by saying I have barely played Runescape, maybe an hour tops, so a lot of this was somewhat new to me. Once you understand the loop of it all, its quite addicting. This being fun to play before bed on the steam deck and getting all of your content for free on the mobile versions is just the cherry on top. Just make sure you have a task running before you log off! I took me a couple days to figure that one out.
It's like playing runescape while using a bot to automate everything. Best idler on the market. I played this for about 2 years before it was on steam.

The best idle game out there. Progression is constant and satisfying. It has a low price with no in-game monetization and purchasing on Steam gives you access to all your content across multiple devices. There are a large variety of ways to tailor the game to your preference: different game modes, mods, playing actively instead of idly, self-imposed rules, etc...

Similar to Runescape in many ways of course. It may not be the type of game that everyone can enjoy, but for those that do enjoy it- there's hundreds to thousands of hours that can be spent on it.

Beautifully executed. There are so many skills and almost all of them are complexly intertwined with each other. The resource and guides for the game are abundant. The devs are responsive. This is one my my favorite games of all time.

tldr.text: Very Positive (92%): players love the content and replay value, and many say the game is worth the price.
The main complaint is the price, and some call the game bland, with little reason to return unless you enjoy grinding.

details.text: Reviews from the last 30 days look much like the all-time picture, at 90% positive.
New players are much less positive (63%) than players with over 50 hours, who make up most of the long-time fans.
